overview: This Senate resolution names July 2026 "American Grown Flower and Foliage Month." It recognizes the farmers in the United States who grow cut flowers and greenery, such as roses, sunflowers, tulips, and eucalyptus, and notes that only a small share of the flowers sold in the country are grown here. It points to the "American Grown Flowers" label created in 2014 to help shoppers find domestic flowers. The resolution urges people to choose and display American-grown flowers to support farmers, small businesses, and the broader agriculture industry. The Senate agreed to it by unanimous consent on July 30, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution draws attention to domestic flower growers and helps consumers who want to buy locally grown products.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not change any law or spending.
